title: K-injective evaluation models on a single scheme site
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a derived category in universe w [def-pc-derived-category], Q its localization, and H its derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let P,F be actual complexes of O_Y-modules [def-pur-hom-complex], F K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], Hom(P,-) preserve every quasi-isomorphism, and V=Hom(P,O_Y[0]) K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let K,N be derived objects with eK:QP isomorphic to K and eN:QF isomorphic to N. Let f:Tot(F tensor V) to Hom(P,F) satisfy [def-pc-scheme-ordinary-evaluation-formula]. Put D=H(K,1), using the shared tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], and let g:N tensor D to H(K,N) be the inverse canonical tensor-Hom bijection [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] applied to associator; N tensor the uncurrying of identity_D; right unitor. There exist isomorphisms a:N tensor D to Q(Tot(F tensor V)) and b:H(K,N) to Q(Hom(P,F)) such that g;b=a;Q(f). Both complexes and both derived functors use the same site and the same localization; there is no exact site-equivalence functor in the statement.

proof.text: The coefficient F is already K-injective. The derived internal Hom factorization identifies its ordinary Hom target with RHom(K,N). Take the fixed functorial K-injective resolution of the degree-zero unit. Hom exactness makes Hom(P,eta_unit) a quasi-isomorphism. The derived internal Hom factorization, its localized inverse, and eK identify the actual ordinary dual with RHom(K,1). These comparison objects are actual Hom complexes, and no arbitrary witness of mere existence defines data.

The K-flat dual computes derived tensor with every F: use symmetry to apply the K-flat first-factor comparison and then restore the order F tensor dual. Compose with eN and the dual comparison of the preceding step to get a. Take b to be the target comparison of that step. All comparison data are used existentially in the proof, not installed as choices in definitions.

Use K-flat resolutions of the tensor inputs and the same fixed K-injective target as the canonical tensor-Hom representative equation. Uncurry the identity of the dual and form its tensor with F. Follow a degree-(p,q) tensor inclusion by the r-th Hom projection. Associator and symmetry restore F tensor dual; evaluating the dual on P^r and acting on F^p by the unit gives the scheme-site hf component when r+q=0, and every other component is zero because the unit is supported in degree zero. Evaluation is natural with the resolution maps. The tensor coproduct inclusions and Hom product projections detect equality of chain maps. Localize that equality and cancel the Hom resolution isomorphisms to obtain the square. This calculation asserts no inverse of f and uses neither boundedness nor finite freeness.

theorem exists_kInjective_scheme_evaluation_models (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (K N : schemeDerivedCategory Y)
    (P F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hhom : ∀ (M M' : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ) (t : M ⟶ M'),
      QuasiIso t → QuasiIso (((homComplexFunctor (R := Y.sheaf)).obj (op P)).map t))
    (hdual : (homComplex (R := Y.sheaf) P
      ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
        (𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))))).IsKFlat)
    (eK : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ K) (eN : DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ N)
    (f : pullbackTensorTotal Y F
        (homComplex (R := Y.sheaf) P
          ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))))) ⟶
      homComplex (R := Y.sheaf) P F)
    (hf : IsSchemeOrdinaryEvaluation Y P F f) [F.IsKInjective] :
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y.toRingedSpace) Y.sheaf
    let D := H.obj (op K, 𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory Y))
    let g := ((schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv Y) (N ⊗ D) K N).symm
      ((α_ N D K).hom ≫ N ◁
        ((schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv Y) D K
          (𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory Y)) (𝟙 D)) ≫ (ρ_ N).hom)
    ∃ a : N ⊗ D ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (pullbackTensorTotal Y F
          (homComplex (R := Y.sheaf) P
            ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
              (𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)))))),
      ∃ b : H.obj (op K, N) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (homComplex (R := Y.sheaf) P F),
        g ≫ b.hom = a.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map f
